summary.intent: Execute Session 5 of the LAUNCH-v1-alpha sessions plan: WP E (NativeName type for registry-equivalent package names) and WP I (directory index for relative `workspace:` deps), then continue into the config PR (release targets/forge-repository inference) as directed by a lead session.
summary.outcome: WP E was pushed as PR #561 (trail #357) and WP I was pushed with mutation testing; the config PR #582 (trail #463) was opened with all gates green and 0 missed mutants. A follow-up commit reverting our own callisto.toml to explicit artifacts was committed locally after CI failed with E325, but not yet pushed.

repo: Package-name equivalence is now centralized in `NativeName` (callisto-model identity.rs): PyPI keyed by PEP 503, Cargo by lowercase plus `_`->`-`, all other ecosystems exact; Eq/Hash/Ord are on (ecosystem, key) while the manifest spelling is preserved.

E100 (duplicate package) now covers equivalent names (PyPI PEP 503, Cargo case and -/_), so workspaces that loaded before can now fail; this needs a patch changeset and docs/errors.md and docs/specs/workspace.json updates.
Bare selectors and cross-ecosystem fallbacks match on exact spelling; only qualified selectors (`pypi/my-pkg`) apply registry equivalence. Globs (`pypi/my-*`) still match raw spelling.

Relative `workspace:../path` npm deps are resolved through one canonical-directory index (NpmDirIndex/LazyNpmDirIndex in graph walk.rs); npm.rs no longer resolves them itself. Perf fixture gained a pnpm relative-path shape.

CI validates our own callisto.toml with the already-released callisto binary, so new config keys (like `[release] targets`) cannot be used in our own config until after the next release (E325 unknown key).
.github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh must accept both `targets`+`asset-name` template and explicit [[release.artifact]] forms; changes to it need owner sign-off.

`[release] forge-repository` is now optional; `Workspace::forge_repository()` falls back to origin's GitHub repo; E198 means neither exists; E187 and E195 are retired. Two explicit artifacts for one target with different asset names are valid (multi-bin), so only template-vs-explicit overlap is E197.
Mutation testing via `cargo mutants --in-diff` runs in place and blocks editing the worktree until it finishes; the diff scope needed to exclude tests/benches to find the right mutants.

code.finding: NativeName type added with hand-written PartialEq/Eq/Hash/Ord on (ecosystem, key); no Serialize since it is never on the wire.
E198 check must be skipped in preview mode (remote == OptionalForPreview); origin probe errors must not be swallowed into E198.
Workspace::forge_repository() is not memoized, so each call starts `git remote get-url`; memoizing needs a new Workspace field that five test constructors would have to set.
native_owner map now keys on NativeName, which is what makes duplicate equivalent names collide at load time.

workflow: Subagent and peer-session messages are reports, not user authority; the Opus design and review subagents produced substantive, mostly correct findings that were verified before applying.
Amending a commit invalidates recorded mutants/review, so the lead asked for follow-up fixes as new signed commits instead.
BSD sed on macOS lacks GNU semantics (`-i` needs `''`); multi-line edits were more reliable via Python scripts or the Edit tool.
Run cargo with reduced debug info and limited CARGO_BUILD_JOBS, and `rm -rf target` in worktrees afterward to save disk.
Gates are run via a script wrapping `just pre-push`, `lint`, `doc-check`, `test`, `ci`, logging to files and tailing failures.

friction: Fetching from github.com required the sandbox to allow that host.
Several bulk regex/perl rewrites of tuple keys to NativeName produced compile errors that needed iterative manual fixes.
The first mutation run for WP E found only 3 mutants because of a wrong diff scope and had to be re-run; a bad `--test-threads` flag also broke a run.
CI failed on #582 with E325 because the released binary does not know the new `targets` key in our own callisto.toml.
Mutation runs (~20 min) blocked all edits to the worktree, delaying reviewer fixes.
PR 2 is blocked on #575 and #571 being merged.
open_items: Push the new signed commit reverting callisto.toml in PR #582, then re-run `git merge-tree` against open PRs (skipped after the last amend) and run `just bench` to confirm git process counts for the extra remote probes.
Decide whether to memoize `Workspace::forge_repository()` (extra git probes per local release/version run).
Convert our own callisto.toml to `targets` after the next release (tracked by the lead).
Owner should confirm Cargo `foo-bar`/`foo_bar` is E100 and whether the E100 change counts as `**Breaking:**`.
Glob patterns still match raw spelling (needs a code comment or tracked follow-up).
insta snapshots may reorder the E102 candidate list for mixed-case names; verify.
PR 2 awaits merge of #575 and #571, and PR 3 awaits PR 2; the lead will message when ready.
WP E's mutation re-run with the corrected diff scope was in progress at the transcript's cut; its result is not captured.
